Options

The living air

Mist sits above the lake. Dust drifts through the sanctuary. The dragon, weapons, and explosions disturb nearby particles. Lens droplets stay near the screen edges.

V: compare air on / off. This changes the added air effects, not the route or combat. The same control is available with the Air strength slider.

Presentation

Auto adjusts resolution from measured frame time. High adds mist layers, more airborne particles, projected water shadows, and longer exhaust trails. Balanced reduces these costs. Lens droplets and the cinematic finish are off by default.

Sound

Two original, embedded music loops and twelve effect cues. Audio unlocks on your first key, click, touch, or controller input.

Flight

Voyager reduces incoming damage. Original is the default balance; Veteran is less forgiving. Linked mode moves the dragon toward the reticle. Difficulty changes apply immediately.

Device

Touch controls appear automatically on touch devices. Landscape is recommended. A standard-mapped controller can navigate menus with the D-pad, A / Cross to select, and B / Circle to go back.

Settings and your best completed score are stored locally when browser storage is available. The boss checkpoint lasts only for this session.

Changes are applied immediately and saved on this device.
The flight manual

Two weapons. Every direction.

You fly forward automatically. Move the dragon to dodge, aim independently, and turn the view to track threats on the radar. Your gun and your dragon’s lasers have different jobs.

The field notes / completion report

Azure Reliquary

2026-09-29   GPT-6 ASTRA PRO   OFFLINE / SINGLE HTML

A complete, self-contained dragon-flight level inspired by Panzer Dragoon for Sega Saturn. This is an unofficial, authored reinterpretation of Episode 1, Ruins of the Lake, not an exact port or a Sega product. All geometry, illustration, interface, code and audio in this file were created for this build.

Important specification deviations. The requested three.js r186 and source-game audio could not be downloaded into the build environment. This file instead uses a custom native WebGPU renderer with automatic WebGL2 fallback, compiled from TypeScript 5.8.3, and original synthesized MP3 music and sound effects. It does not contain three.js, Vite, Rapier, Sega music, or extracted Sega sound effects. The required stack and source-audio portions of the brief are therefore not fulfilled.

Graphics pass 02 — The living air

Built September 29, 2026 · GPT-6 Astra Pro. This pass changes the environment and effects. It keeps the complete level, combat, controls, checkpoints, and results from the first build.

Open water: low mist, wind-driven spray, sunlight in haze, water ripples, contact foam, and a low-flight wake. Wet stone has algae stains, mineral streaks, and moving water light. Broken arches, reeds, torn banners, and falling water add local motion.

Sanctuary: cooler shade, dust in light from roof gaps, damp walls, blue lamp glow, and fine water streams. The collapse releases a bounded dust cloud. Warship: engine exhaust, damage smoke, a moving pennant, sagging cables, and torpedo spray.

Response to play: the dragon disturbs nearby motes and leaves short wingtip trails. Laser launches and explosions light nearby surfaces. Gunfire aimed at the water makes spray and rings.

Controls: use Options → The living air to set air strength, dust and spray, light beams, and lens droplets. Press V to compare air on and off. Lens droplets are off by default. They stay near the edges when enabled.

Technical limits: this is still the first build’s custom native WebGPU / WebGL2 stack, not three.js r186. Mist and beams use layered, depth-tested geometry. They are not full volumetric simulation. Cloth, cables, water reflections, and wakes are bounded visual approximations. The original synthesized audio is unchanged.

Hub migration: the new Atmosphere module is separate from gameplay. It receives route, player, and combat events through the Host interface. It adds one sorted, instanced transparent pass. Port the shared noise sampling and shaders to TSL and use the hub’s quality and input services. The TypeScript source is embedded in atmosphere-typescript.

Second-pass tests — September 29, 2026: strict TypeScript compilation passed. Chromium 144 / WebGL2 completed the full level with all 50 counted targets destroyed, an eight-target volley, and 15 gun interceptions. The automated run used movement and weapon inputs, without health edits or direct kill calls. A separate boss-cycle test covered all four sectors and the delayed torpedoes. Defeat and the visible checkpoint-retry button worked.

Effects and controls: the air slider, V comparison, particle and beam switches, and optional lens droplets were checked. Balanced / High used 86 / 180 ambient motes and capped burst particles at 34 / 70. Burst particles and impact rings expired in the cleanup test. A separate draw check removed the air layers when air strength was zero. Shadows remain a separate setting. Keyboard/mouse, a simulated standard gamepad, and synthetic multi-touch passed. Portrait and landscape layouts were inspected.

Runtime checks and limits: all 14 embedded MP3 assets decoded. The tested pages made zero network requests and reported no uncaught or console errors. A simulated WebGPU-adapter failure selected WebGL2. Tests ran as inline page content because browser policy blocked file-URL navigation. Native WebGPU, direct local-file launch, saved-data persistence across local-file reloads, physical controllers, and target-device frame rates remain unverified. A steady 60 fps on Galaxy S25 or RTX 3060 is not certified.

Launch instructions

Open this HTML file directly in a current browser with hardware acceleration and either WebGPU or WebGL2. No installation, server, connection, or additional file is needed. Select Begin the flight. Audio unlocks on first interaction. For mobile, open the file in the browser itself rather than a document-preview application; rotate to landscape. The browser or operating system may limit local-file launch, fullscreen, gamepad access, or local storage.

Use Flight manual for all three control schemes. Escape / P pauses. Default settings use separate movement and aim, generous acquisition, and the Original difficulty. The encounter does not time out: destroy the warship to finish. A full run consists of a 158-second approach, the boss fight, and an eight-second departure. The boss retry checkpoint is an added convenience, not a source-game feature.

Systems and implementation

The route automatically advances while the rider and dragon move across the flight plane. Four smoothly transitioning quarter-turn views share a 360-degree radar. Rapid gun fire uses projected hit regions and resolves nearer targets first. Hold-to-mark lasers acquire up to eight distinct targets, display persistent marks, then fly in curving volleys on release. Lasers do not intercept hostile ordnance. Repeated volleys are needed against armor. Lock acquisition intentionally ignores scenery, preserving the guide’s through-wall targeting.

The boss has shared hull health across three wide engine targets. Gunners can be temporarily suppressed and recover. The ship moves through all four viewing sectors; its left-side phase drops three delayed-launch torpedoes. Survival, scoring, kill ratio, gun accuracy, intercept count, hit chains, failure, full retry, checkpoint retry and victory are implemented. A separate projectile color and outline make hostile shots readable.

Clearly separated additions

New content: the title, procedural art, music, reconstructed geography, staged ruin collapse, additional port and rear formations, boss engine weak points, all exact timings, scoring values and difficulty balance. Modern conveniences: independent move/aim with optional classic linked mode, larger acquisition regions, rear/front shortcuts, three difficulty settings, checkpoint retry, local records, touch controls, controller menu navigation, audio sliders, fullscreen, automatic pause on focus loss, and the measured quality system. No claim is made that the original has these interfaces or exact values.

Intentionally outside this slice

The other episodes, the full introductory cinematic, later bosses, the complete Tower narrative, source-game training mode and original unlockable modes are not included. There is no campaign save, currency, inventory, collectible, upgrade tree, free-roaming flight, or online service. No progression outside this level is implied.

Research and source distinction

The Panzer Dragoon game reference supports the rail-flight, two-weapon and four-view core. The Naraka reference informed the interception. Ollie Barder’s remake review informed the independently adjustable aiming and generous lock-on area. Official r186 release notes were verified, but the package could not be installed. Archive or reference links are optional documentation links; the game never requests them.

First-build verification record

Verified September 29, 2026: strict TypeScript compilation; Chromium 144 rendering with the WebGL2 software backend; successful decoding of all 14 embedded MP3 assets; no external runtime requests or uncaught errors in the tested page. An automated fixed-step playthrough completed all 14 formations and the boss, destroyed all 50 counted targets, exercised all four boss sectors and the three delayed torpedoes, and reached victory in 3 minutes 21 seconds. A simulated WebGPU-adapter failure correctly fell back to WebGL2. Separate checks covered defeat, the visible boss-checkpoint retry button, all four views, eight-target lock capacity, two-hit armored enemies, gun interception, keyboard/mouse input, a simulated standard-mapped gamepad, synthetic multi-touch, input cancellation, and measured Auto / High / Balanced budgets. Title, gameplay, controls, options and results were visually inspected in desktop and mobile-sized layouts. Verification limits: browser policy blocked file-URL navigation, so the embedded HTML was executed as inline page content instead; direct local-file launch and saved-data persistence across local-file reloads were not verified. Native WebGPU was unavailable in this test context and has not been runtime-validated. No physical gamepad, Samsung Galaxy S25 or RTX 3060 benchmark was performed; 60 fps on target hardware is not certified.

Architecture and creature silhouettes are authored low-poly interpretations, not exact Saturn assets. The water reflects a procedural sky, not the scene. Shadows are flat analytic projections, not shadow maps. There are no rigid bodies: collision uses simple deterministic radii, height ranges and projected targeting. Decorative out-of-lane ruins are not all colliders. Aim-at-screen targeting is intentionally permissive, including through-wall locks. Audio loops have brief composed fade boundaries. Fullscreen, touch file launching and storage support depend on the browser.

Graphics-device loss pauses the game and requests a reload; it does not hot-swap a lost live device. Best scores are not segregated by difficulty, and changing difficulty mid-run is allowed. The checkpoint preserves approach score and kills, but starts fresh boss-attempt accuracy, intercept and chain statistics. This is a replayable level adaptation, not a bit-accurate simulation.

Hub migration notes

The transpiled namespaces retain three explicit boundaries: ReliquaryEngine owns renderer boot/fallback, geometry batching, input, audio and quality; AzureGame.Game consumes the Host interface; ReliquaryApp owns loading, fixed-step scheduling, menus and DOM feedback. The uncompiled TypeScript is embedded in inert source blocks for inspection and migration. No runtime package, CDN, WASM, external font or fetched asset is used.

Material migration work remains: replace the custom renderer and its native WGSL/GLSL shaders with hub-provided three.js r186 WebGPURenderer and TSL materials. Convert scene instances and custom matrix/vector utilities to the hub engine. Replace the current TypeScript-only compile with the hub’s Vite build. Input, audio manifest and quality controls are separated, but currently use concrete local engine types rather than imported hub modules. There are no copied library files or external imports because there are no third-party runtime libraries. The code consequently does not satisfy the requested bare-import stack convention.

Simulation runs at a fixed 60 Hz with an accumulator, catch-up cap and interpolated transforms. Rapier is not used because rail motion, bullets and simple obstacles require no rigid-body simulation; the active rigid-body count is always zero. High / Balanced use particle caps of 180 / 75 and projectile caps of 80 / 48, with entity lifetimes and removal. Auto chooses between these budgets and changes drawing resolution from measured frame time rather than device names. Screen-edge shading starts disabled. High adds more mist layers, more ambient particles, more projected shadows, and longer exhaust trails.
